title: Adrian Gore's 1992 To-Do List: 'Come Up With Ideas'
conflicts: The slate's 'single idea' framing is wrong: Discovery's own history says Gore arrived at RMB with an exam pad of ideas and a to-do item to come up with products, the medical savings account following by February 1993; story follows the company record. Start date: 10 March 1992 (Discovery newsroom) vs Gore telling Forbes the health insurer was developed in 1993; story uses 1992 for the start and 1993 for the first trading year. Age: 'mid-20s' (Brunswick interviewer) vs 27 from his 1964 birth date; story says 27. R10 million seed capital comes from the Brunswick interviewer and CNBC Africa, not a primary document. Listing year: about 1999 implied by Brunswick vs 1997 (KDSF); story avoids a listing year. Early figures (3,300 lives, about R1 million premiums, profit in 1995, 1,000+ staff in 1998) are Discovery's own and attributed.
notes: Company is given as 'Momentum Health (later Discovery Health)' because that was its name until October 1998. Funding changed from the slate's 'mixed' to 'venture' (seed money from Dippenaar and RMB's founders). Daily Investor's fuller account (Dippenaar asking for a rethink, paying Gore's salary) is blocked and was not used. Stance: complicates.
